decisions.question: What is the baseline each lap is compared against? A: a neutral reference - fuel AND tyre-compound effects taken out once, and track rubber/temperature NOT taken out a second time. B: what the field actually did that day, with nothing subtracted again.
decisions.context: F22 (rubber+ambient) and F38 (compound) are one defect - a component the base already contains, subtracted again - so they need one answer, not two. A matches how fuel is already handled and needs no new design work. B changes what the residual MEANS (pace vs what the field actually did) and would force re-justifying the residual's header identity and 07's closed-channel causal argument from scratch.
decisions.resolution: A (neutral baseline): fuel AND tyre-compound effects taken out once, track rubber/temperature NOT taken out again. Matches existing fuel handling.

decisions.question: What happens to safety-car / VSC / red-flag / restart laps (9,016 of 139,947 eligible training rows, 6.4%) at training time? Exclude them outright, or keep them at reduced weight via correction_weight (computed today, applied nowhere in ml/src)?
decisions.context: Either way the same rule has to reach int_field_pace_curve's eligibility CTE, because these laps also enter the field-pace baseline F1 depends on. Weighting keeps more data and matches what correction_weight was built for; excluding is a one-line change that mirrors how 'mistake' and 'conditions' laps are already handled. The audit's own write-up leans to weighting.
decisions.recommendation: Orchestrator's read, not the audit's: exclude. Those laps are slow because the field is queueing behind the safety car, not because tyres wore, so a reduced weight still trains on a label that is not degradation.
decisions.resolution: Exclude, extended to lap-after-restart: per-agent measurement, SC laps do not wear tyres measurably (queueing effect only, ~0.25s thermal lag); restart laps already excluded but lap-after-restart carries systematically wrong labels (-5.1s fake recovery) and must be excluded (1,588 training rows). Also exclude yellow-flag pre-deployment laps. This removes ~10.2k rows (7.4%) instead of 8.6k. Serving unaffected (out-of-envelope laps already flagged).

decisions.question: Compound-seed leakage: refit the seed point-in-time (each season fitted only on earlier seasons), or declare a same-race exemption and make training match serving?
decisions.context: Leaving it as-is (train on in-race fitted values, serve on carried-forward ones) is not an option: it makes every pre-2025 headline optimistic relative to what the model does on an unrun race. Measured cost of the honest option (arm C): small (~0.7%) on the trio and cliff, but -0.0761 AFT NLL (~3.8%) on stint-life.
decisions.recommendation: Orchestrator's read, not the audit's: point-in-time - it is what the model does at serving time and follows int_sc_hazard_history's precedent - accepting the stint-life cost knowingly, since D5 tunes against that family.
decisions.resolution: A: Point-in-time refit. Accept the -3.8% stint-life cost; D5 is tuned against that family anyway. Honest at serving time.

decisions.question: Which season is the holdout? No completed season is unspent (2025 was consumed as a selection fold by 02c's admission gate). Pin 2026 explicitly and fill it with the races run so far, or declare that no clean holdout exists yet?
decisions.context: Today resolve_holdout_season returns MAX(race_year)+1, which is 2026 with 0 rows, and it moves the moment data arrives, so it can never hold rows. The card, README, HOLDOUT_NOTE and a tautological test all describe the mechanism as working. FASTF1 CHECK 2026-09-25 (agent-run): as of 2026-09-25 rounds 1-14 are complete and FastF1 has every input the repo ingests for all 14 races and qualifying sessions, except Monaco (rd 6: position channel truncated at source, telemetry merges on 128 of 1,452 laps) and circuit_info for rd 6 and rd 14 (Madrid: MultiViewer 404, the repo tolerates that). None of the 14 is in bronze (no season=2026 folder anywhere). Ingest is per round (`ingestion/src/ingest.py --season 2026 --round N --session both`), not the whole-season form, which would loop into unrun rounds 15-23; about 35-40 min, ~1.4 GB of FastF1 cache, ~0.65 GB of bronze. The non-FastF1 seeds have 0 rows for 2026 (race_to_track, race_scheduled_laps, tyre_allocations, raw_dim_events), which is WI-05's onboarding gate. Miami's first load silently returned no points/grid from Ergast; ingest skips a race whose laps file exists, so re-run with --force if a load looks thin. Round 15 (Baku) qualifies 2026-09-25 and races 2026-09-26.
decisions.recommendation: Orchestrator's read, not the audit's: pin holdout_season = 2026 in config, state holdout_populated: false until 2026 rows exist, and ingest the 2026 races already run if the data is available - the only option that yields a clean holdout rather than a declared absence.
decisions.resolution: Pin 2026 as holdout season. Set holdout_populated = false for now. Use 2026 as the holdout to measure performance as the season progresses; ingest 2026 data incrementally as races complete rather than upfront. This unblocks WI-03 (Holdout policy).

decisions.question: Equal-car teammate rating: compare P20 against P20 (keeps the 'kill cruise drag' ceiling logic, applied on both sides), or median against median (simpler, loses the ceiling)?
decisions.context: Today one side is a ceiling and the other a mean, so more lap-time scatter reads as faster: mean teammate pair sum is -1.83s and 79% of two-driver cars rate both teammates faster than each other. The choice feeds F44 and F45 downstream.
decisions.recommendation: P20-vs-P20 (the WI doc's recommendation): the smaller conceptual change, and it preserves the model header's stated intent.
decisions.note_2026_09_28: User deferred: needs a design and experiment round before deciding. WI-14b stays blocked.

decisions.question: About 9% of 2018 laps (about 1,450 training rows) have no telemetry, and the pipeline records them as 'clear air, no traffic', a guess presented as a measurement. What should 'fixed' mean? A: keep the guess, guard it with a per-season check (WI-07's T15). B: record 'unknown' (NULL) instead of the guess. C: drop those laps from training.
decisions.context: Every other season is at about 0%. B flows into the dirty-air cost and both labels, so it is a label change and rides WI-01's version bump. C is a training-set change. The verify_findings F12 check measures NULL gap_ahead_min_s, which no COALESCE edit changes, so under A or C the check itself has to be redefined. FASTF1 CHECK 2026-09-25 (agent-run, orchestrator spot-checked bronze and the mart): the gap is exactly two whole races, 2018_1 Australia (720 rows) and 2018_2 Bahrain (731 rows), 1,451 of 15,806; every other 2018 race has 0 NULL. It is at the SOURCE, not our bronze: FastF1 has no position channel for either race (Australia has the car channel only; Bahrain has neither), and the raw archive returns 403 for those streams, so re-ingesting cannot change the 9.18%. C therefore means dropping two specific races' laps. ADR-009 / data-schemas.mdx:35 overstate it (the archive does hold Australia's race car stream). Nothing here changes A/B/C; it removes 're-pull the data' as a fourth option.
decisions.recommendation: Orchestrator's read: B, folded into WI-01's bump, plus A's guard now (WI-07's T15) so it cannot regress meanwhile.
decisions.resolution: B: Record NULL instead of the guess. Honest. Moves dirty-air cost and both labels (rides WI-01's version bump). Plus A's guard (WI-07's T15) to prevent regression.

decisions.question: P3.1 gate failure at Monza HARD: accept as a known edge case or require a level-offset term first?
decisions.context: The model measures real tyre wear correctly (0.24s error against actual wear). The gate's 'truth' is biased by ~0.9s due to baseline car mix (2024 race dominates, Ferrari/RBR faster in 2023). Per-race fits also fail there (0.98s). The fixture also has stale data (W54).
decisions.resolution: Accept Monza HARD as a known edge case. The test marks it `it.fails` to keep CI green without hiding the gap. The model is sound; the baseline is the issue (separate work if you want to fix it later). Move WI-17 to LANDED.

watch_vocabulary.ship-blocker: Publishing or shipping without this breaks something users see. `board.py --ship` exits 1 while one is open.
watch_vocabulary.hazard: A standing trap that damages tracked files or results if someone does the obvious thing. Read before running anything nearby.
watch_vocabulary.uncommitted: Verified work that lives only in the working tree. Committing is the user's call.
watch_vocabulary.unreviewed: Changes in the working tree that no orchestrator has read or tested. Not to be built on until reviewed.
watch_vocabulary.unverified: A claim or code path that was run in one place only (dev but not CI, agent report but not re-run).
watch_vocabulary.stale-artifact: A built or generated thing that no longer matches the source it came from until it is rebuilt.
watch_vocabulary.pending-ruling: A question for the human that is not (yet) a blocking FD: it changes a note, a value or a scope, not an item's ability to run.
watch_vocabulary.gate-gap: A guard that does not guard: it errors, skips files silently, or cannot fail.
watch_vocabulary.debt: Known, documented, deliberately left. Each needs an owner eventually.

watch_model_vocabulary.haiku: Maps to haiku-4-5. A binary check, or recording a resolution the evidence or the user has already settled: is it committed, did the named tests pass on the rebuild, write down the accept. The output has a mechanical check (a test result, a file list, git log).
watch_model_vocabulary.sonnet: Maps to sonnet-5. The fix or the options are written down in the rule: pick between two named options, run a named rebuild or export and check the pages, review a diff, reconcile counts, reword text to a meaning already settled.
watch_model_vocabulary.opus: Maps to opus-5 (fable-5.1 if the rule turns into a new estimator). Rules on a trade-off, designs the fix, audits a decision, or turns a measurement into a claim: label-moving changes, leakage boundaries, gate runs before a promotion.

watch_rules.title: 08o's 'uniform beats IPW' no longer holds on the corrected weights: revisit before the v15 retrain?
watch_rules.detail: The W9 re-run (2026-09-29) used the corrected survival_weight on today's substrate, and it reverses most of the evidence 08o dropped IPW on in v13. Corrected season-lagged IPW beats uniform on p50 (+1.78x floor; the alignment information term has E=1589, n=10) and, marginally, on p10 (+1.01x, E=27). Uniform still wins p90 (-0.98x, inside the floor). The shipped v13/v14 models are unaffected: they are uniform and were trained on the old substrate. This bears on what the v15 retrain on WI-01's label should use. Caveats: one eval season (2025, cv_final_fold), and the floor measures seed noise only. The e-values are single contrasts per head. Arm A is uniform-as-ones, which is not bit-identical to production w=None. Against w=None, IPW is +0.65x/+2.60x/-1.06x. If IPW returns, W10 (the value for long-stint tail cells, 1.0 vs 4.0) becomes live, and so does the per-head question (p90 goes the other way).
watch_rules.clears_when: The user rules: keep uniform for v15 and record why, or re-gate IPW for the quantile heads as part of the v15 retrain (settling W10 with it).
watch_rules.resolution:
RE-GATED AS PART OF THE v15 RETRAIN (user instruction, 2026-09-29). RECOMMENDATION: KEEP UNIFORM (w=None, the v14 configuration) FOR v15. IPW's gain is real on 2025 but does not hold across seasons, and IPW makes p90 worse in every season. Nothing needs flipping: the new switch defaults to uniform.

How: all five models were retrained at v14's *_best_params.json (no re-tune, so the weight is the only thing that moves). They used the W9 isolated warehouse (gate_after.duckdb, whose transform tree is byte-identical to today's working tree; dev.duckdb was not opened). Training covers 2018-2025, with 85,859 trio rows. New opt-in switch ML_QUANTILE_WEIGHT=none|ipw (schema.QUANTILE_SAMPLE_WEIGHT), read by train._sample_weight and evaluate._row_weights. It defaults to none, so production is unchanged, and training logs now record sample_weight_scheme. Artefacts are ml/models/*_v15ipw.{bst,onnx} and *_v15uni.{bst,onnx} (gitignored; all 10 pass ONNX parity). The v14 files, encoders.json, manifest.json and ml/artefacts/evaluation_metrics.json are unchanged. The comparator is uniform rebuilt on the new label, not published v14: v14 is on the pre-WI-01 label and was trained on 2025, so re-scoring it on 2025 would be in-sample. The 2025 refits reproduce the W9 re-run exactly: uniform 0.5867/0.9605/0.4343 = 08o production, IPW 0.5824/0.9483/0.4394 = 08o arm B. Evidence is in _roadmap/_fixes/_evidence/w58-2026-09-29/ (w58_v15_compare.py, eval_uniform.json, eval_ipw.json, arms.json, boosters.json, w58_v15_summary.json, w58_v15_report.log, PROVENANCE.txt).

Pinball, lower is better. change = uniform minus IPW, as a share of uniform; positive = IPW better.
| Head | 2025 uniform (v14 config) | 2025 IPW (v15ipw) | change | x seed floor (10 paired seeds) | 5-fold uniform | 5-fold IPW | change | seasons IPW won | paired t p |
| p10 | 0.5867 | 0.5824 | +0.73% | +0.64x (IPW better 10/10) | 0.4381 | 0.4370 | +0.19% | 4/5 | 0.43 |
| p50 | 0.9605 | 0.9483 | +1.27% | +2.90x (10/10, E=8,044) | 0.8867 | 0.8853 | +0.15% | 3/5 | 0.62 |
| p90 | 0.4343 | 0.4394 | -1.17% | -1.06x (1/10) | 0.4597 | 0.4620 | -0.49% | 0/5 | 0.11 |
| trio CRPS | 1.3810 | 1.3717 | +0.7% | | 1.2473 | 1.2487 | -0.1% | | |
| [p10,p90] coverage (nominal 0.80) | 0.755 | 0.759 | | | 0.767 | 0.770 | | | |
5-fold = validate on 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 (expanding window), 3 seeds per fold, seed-averaged. Published v14 on the old label, for reference only: 0.388/0.861/0.483.

Reading: on 2025 the p50 gain is well outside seed noise, so it is real for that season, but seasons vary by more than the effect. 2024 reverses it (p50 0.9169 uniform vs 0.9225 IPW). Over five seasons the 95% CIs for p10 and p50 both span zero ([-0.0024, +0.0045] and [-0.0062, +0.0091]). p90 loses in all five seasons. The 2025 breakdown shows the mechanism: IPW helps p50 on long stints (laps 21-30 +0.021, 31+ +0.025) and on MEDIUM (+0.025), but costs p90 on the same laps (31+ -0.035). A per-head mix (IPW p10/p50, uniform p90) has the best five-fold CRPS, by 0.1% (1.2461 vs 1.2473), which does not justify a per-head switch. W10 measured: setting the 1,769 tail rows (1,734 of 2019, 35 of 2024) to 4.0 instead of 1.0 moves every head by at most 0.001 (p >= 0.18). That is immaterial either way, and moot under uniform. Cost is neutral: same fit time, IPW boosters about 3% fewer leaves, ONNX size and latency equal within timing noise. cliff_classifier and stint_life_regressor are byte-identical across arms because they do not read the weight. Promoting v15 is separate work: rebuild dev, bump MODEL_VERSION_DEFAULT, run make ml-retrain, ml-evaluate, ml-onnx and ml-card, and respect W25's re-export gating.
